::: {#exr-miller-deriv-second-log-constant}
#### Second derivative with an added constant

Find the second derivative of

$$f(x) = \log x + \sqrt{162}$$

for $x > 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-second-log-constant}
Because $\sqrt{162}$ is constant with respect to $x$, its derivative is zero (@thm-deriv-const):

$$f'(x) = \frac{1}{x} = x^{-1}$$

Differentiating again via the power rule (@thm-deriv-polynomial):

$$f''(x) = -x^{-2} = -\frac{1}{x^2}$$
:::
